unmapped: Cascade feedback: learner observes only the index of the first chosen item whose weight is zero (items before it are observed)
Non-linear (conjunctive, product) reward: reward is 1 iff all chosen items have weight 1
Item weights are independent Bernoulli (factored distribution P)
Actions are ordered tuples of distinct ground items from an arbitrary feasible set Theta
settings.definition_quote: A combinatorial cascading bandit is a tuple $B = (E, P, \Theta)$ ... receives a binary reward $\rnd{r}_t = \min_{e \in \rnd{A}_t} \rnd{w}_t(e)$ ... At the end of time $t$, the agent observes the index of the first item in $\rnd{A}_t$ whose weight is zero ... $P(w) = \prod_{e \in E} P_e(w(e))$, where $P_e$ is a Bernoulli distribution with mean $\bar{w}(e)$.

symbols.f_star: expected reward of the optimal solution, f(A*, w_bar) = prod_{e in A*} w_bar(e)
symbols.Delta_e_min: minimum gap of suboptimal solutions containing suboptimal item e
symbols.m: paper's K: maximum number of items in any feasible solution

conditions: optimal solution A* unique as a set
algorithm initialized with one sample w_0 ~ P
tuning: confidence radius c_{t,s} = sqrt(1.5 log t / s)

source.label: thm:ucb1
source.quote: The regret of $\combcascade$ is bounded as $\displaystyle R(n) \leq \frac{K}{f^\ast} \sum_{e \in \tilde{E}} \frac{4272}{\Delta_{e, \min}} \log n + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L$.

results.notes: sum_subopt here sums over suboptimal ground items (E minus A*), not arms. Regret E[sum f(A*,w_t)-f(A_t,w_t)] equals pseudo-regret. Also applies to disjunctive variant with redefined gaps and f*.

source.label: thm:gap-free
source.quote: The regret of $\combcascade$ is bounded as $\displaystyle R(n) \leq 131 \sqrt{\frac{K L n \log n}{f^\ast}} + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L$.

results.notes: Bound still depends on instance through f*; the epsilon in the proof is analysis-only so algorithm does not need n.
